## What SPHEREx is
SPHEREx stands for Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer. It is a NASA Astrophysics mission, selected as a Medium Explorer in February 2019 and launched in March 2025. NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory manages the mission, Caltech is home to the principal investigator and developed the payload, BAE Systems built the spacecraft, and the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute (KASI) is an instrument and science partner. The data are processed and archived at IPAC at Caltech. SPHEREx is an all-sky survey telescope that observes in near-infrared light, from 0.75 to 5.0 micron.
Sources: spherex-about, nasa-spherex-brown-dwarfs, spherex-user-guide, spherex-goals

## Science goals
SPHEREx has three science goals. (1) Constrain the physics of cosmic inflation by measuring its imprint on the three-dimensional large-scale distribution of matter. (2) Trace the history of light production by galaxies through a deep multi-band measurement of large-scale clustering. (3) Investigate the abundance and composition of water and biogenic ices in the early phases of star and planetary-disk formation.
Sources: spherex-goals

## Survey design
SPHEREx collects near-infrared spectra from 0.75 to 5.0 micron over the entire sky, with a measurement about every 6 arcseconds. It maps the full sky four times during its nominal 25-month mission, which is about one all-sky map every six months. NASA describes the result as a map in 102 colors, each color being a different wavelength of light. Spectroscopy splits light into its wavelengths, as a prism does.
Sources: spherex-goals, spherex-about, spherex-user-guide, jpl-spherex-presskit

## Four kinds of statement to keep apart
When talking about SPHEREx, four things must not be mixed up. Instrument specifications describe what the telescope is designed to do (for example the 0.75-5.0 micron range). Archive metadata describe one file (its date, detector, wavelength limits, download address). Measured values are numbers read from the data themselves (a surface brightness in MJy/sr at one pixel). Scientific interpretations are conclusions someone draws from measurements. Q-FIT labels which of the four a statement is.
Sources: qfit-spec
